keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, -1649..-1582: the Theban region. Infobox 'Capital: Thebes', 'ruled the Theban region in Upper Egypt'; under Nebiriau I (1627-1601) 'the realm controlled by the 16th Dynasty extended at least as far north as Hu', and the Second Intermediate Period page adds 'south to Edfu'. The page gives no area.

correction.text: do not use the Delta shape; use new keyframe -1649 (the Theban region, -1649..-1582)

keyframe_review.note: -1600..-1501, 24,559 km2, bbox 29.2-31.5 N, 30.7-32.8 E: the eastern Delta around Avaris and Memphis, 600 km north of Thebes and drawn fifty years after the dynasty ended (1582). The page puts the dynasty at Thebes ('Capital: Thebes'; 'ruled the Theban region in Upper Egypt'); the page does not mention Memphis or the Delta for this dynasty and places the Hyksos at Avaris. Even the vassal reading (von Beckerath, Helck) gives no Delta land. The shape is the Hyksos core, which the Fifteenth Dynasty and Hyksos dossiers draw.

region.text: the Theban region in Upper Egypt

ledger.note: 1649: the Sixteenth Dynasty rules from Thebes. Infobox 'Established: 1649 BC', 'Capital: Thebes'; it 'ruled the Theban region in Upper Egypt'. The Second Intermediate Period page dates the dynasty c. 1650-1580.

c. 1630: war with the Hyksos begins. 'The continuing war against 15th Dynasty dominated the short-lived 16th Dynasty'; 'The armies of the 15th Dynasty, winning town after town'. The year is the Fifteenth Dynasty page's ('after a period of about 20 years since its foundation, extended its rule as far south as Thebes'); this page is undated.

c. 1582: the Sixteenth Dynasty is absorbed. Infobox 'Disestablished: 1582 BC'; Second Intermediate Period page: 'Sometime around 1580 BC, the 16th Dynasty was subsumed after conflict between Thebes and Avaris'. 'eventually threatening and then conquering Thebes itself' is the page's wording; the Seventeenth Dynasty nonetheless holds Thebes from c. 1580.

c. 1582: the Sixteenth Dynasty gives way to the Seventeenth at Thebes. Infobox 'Disestablished: 1582 BC' and 'Succeeded by Seventeenth Dynasty of Egypt' ('Established: c. 1580 BC' on that page). The Turin canon's last entry is five lost kings, 1588-1582.

wars.name: Hyksos-Theban conflict under the Sixteenth Dynasty
wars.outcome: The Hyksos press the Thebans 'town after town'; the page does not date a battle or a treaty (Ryholt: Dedumose I 'sued for a truce in the latter years of the dynasty'); the dynasty is subsumed c. 1582-1580.
wars.note: The page also records the view that the 16th Dynasty comprised vassals of the Hyksos (von Beckerath, Helck): then there is no war, only subordination; not drawn.

certainty.note: Only two limits are named, Hu in the north and Edfu in the south, and only for Nebiriau I's reign; everything else is approximate.

notes:
Cliopatria's shape for this row (eastern Delta, around Avaris) contradicts the pages, which put the dynasty at Thebes; it is marked wrong and replaced by a Theban-region keyframe. Cliopatria seems to follow the 'shepherd kings' reading (Africanus, via Manetho) in which the 16th are Hyksos; the page gives no land in the Delta for that reading either.
Scholarly views not drawn: the 16th as Hyksos vassals (von Beckerath, Helck); the 16th as a Theban dynasty (Ryholt 1997, Bourriau 2003: the reading drawn). The Abydos Dynasty (c. 1640-1620, local Upper Egyptian kinglets, Second Intermediate Period page) overlaps the Theban realm and needs a dossier or a decision (suggested slug abydos-dynasty).
Page conflicts: the infobox 'Preceded by Fourteenth and Thirteenth' versus the footer 'Preceded by Fifteenth Dynasty'; the dynasty ends 1582 (infobox) or c. 1580 (Second Intermediate Period page); the Turin entries run 1588-1582. The Hyksos hold on Thebes is contradicted between pages (see the Fifteenth Dynasty dossier). The ruler strip follows Ryholt's list as the page gives it, with reigns adjusted to whole years.
Infobox area: none on any page opened, so Cliopatria's 24,559 km2 could not be compared; the Theban radius covers roughly 31,000 km2 before the gazetteer clips it to the valley.
